title: Sample: Network & Server Simulation
description: Original sample covering every question kind, with image exhibits, hotspots and a case study.

caseStudies.title: Case study: Branch office
caseStudies.scenario:
**Overview.** A branch office connects to the internet through firewall FW1. Router R1 routes between the LAN and the firewall. Switch SW1 carries two VLANs: VLAN 10 for users (DHCP) and VLAN 20 for servers.

**Problem.** Users on PC-A report they can't reach the internet, but they can reach SRV1.

**Requirements.**
- Keep VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 separated.
- Only FW1 should translate addresses to the public range.

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end delivery, segmentation and ports?
questions.explanation: Layer 4 (Transport) handles segmentation and process-to-process delivery using **ports**, e.g. TCP and UDP.

questions.prompt: Which of these are RFC 1918 private IPv4 ranges? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The private ranges are 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16. 169.254/16 is link-local (APIPA).
UDP is connectionless and has no retransmission; TCP provides reliability.

questions.prompt: You need to perform the initial configuration of the new switch with a rollover cable. **Click the port you should use.**
questions.explanation: Out-of-box configuration uses the **console** port and a rollover (console) cable.

questions.prompt: The server must be managed out-of-band even when the OS is down. **Click the port to cable to the management network.**
questions.explanation: The dedicated **MGMT** port belongs to the baseboard management controller, which works independently of the host OS.

questions.prompt: Move the DHCP messages to the answer area in the order they are sent. Not all messages are used.
questions.explanation: Discover → Offer → Request → Acknowledge (DORA). Release and Inform are not part of lease acquisition.

questions.prompt: Drag each protocol to its default port. Each port may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
Enter the full IOS command, from privileged EXEC mode, that displays the IPv4 routing table.
questions.explanation: `show ip route` (abbreviations such as `sh ip ro` are accepted).

questions.prompt: A host has address `172.16.45.130/26`. Fill in the values.
questions.explanation: /26 = 64 addresses per block. 130 falls in 128–191, so network .128, broadcast .191, 62 usable hosts.

questions.prompt: Complete the extended ACL entry so hosts in 10.0.10.0/24 can reach SRV1 over HTTPS only.

exhibits.title: Partial ACL
exhibits.text:
ip access-list extended WEB-ONLY
  [action] tcp 10.0.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.20.10 eq [port]
  deny ip any any log

questions.prompt: For each statement, select **Yes** if the statement is true. Otherwise, select **No**.

statements.text: R1's LAN-facing interface Gi0/0 is up/up.
Gi0/1 is down because of a cabling fault.
PC-A and SRV1 are in the same VLAN.

questions.explanation: Gi0/1 is **administratively down** (shut down in config), not a cabling fault. PC-A is in VLAN 10 and SRV1 in VLAN 20.

questions.prompt: Per the requirements, which device should perform NAT to the public range? **Click it in the exhibit.**
questions.explanation: The requirements say only FW1 translates to the public range.

questions.prompt: What should you check first to restore internet access for PC-A?

choices.text: The default route on R1 toward FW1

questions.explanation: Local traffic works but internet traffic doesn't, which points at R1's path to the firewall.
